title: ₹300 Crore, Zombies, and a Phone Call: Inside Ranveer Singh's Wildest Bet Yet
excerpt: Pralay pairs the Dhurandhar superstar with Lokah's Kalyani Priyadarshan for India's first mega-budget post-apocalyptic thriller — and shooting starts next month.
body:
The last time **Ranveer Singh** took a creative risk this big, he walked onto the set of *Dhurandhar* and came back with a film that rewrote every box office record Hindi cinema had. Now he's doing something arguably crazier: he's spending ₹300 crore to bring zombies to Bollywood.

**Pralay**, a post-apocalyptic survival thriller directed by **Jai Mehta**, is scheduled to go on floors in August 2026 — and it is, by every measure, the most ambitious genre film India has ever attempted. Think *World War Z* meets *I Am Legend*, transplanted into a uniquely Indian emotional register: a man fighting through an undead apocalypse to save his family.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=P-X1FXkL8Fk</youtube>


It also happens to be Ranveer's debut as a producer. His banner, **Maa Kasam Films**, is co-producing with **Hansal Mehta's True Story Films** and **Sameer Nair's Applause Entertainment**. For a first production, the man chose maximum chaos. On-brand.

## The Call That Changed Everything

But the story behind the casting might be even better than the film's premise. **Kalyani Priyadarshan** — the South Indian actress who turned the Malayalam fantasy thriller *Lokah: Chapter 1 – Chandra* into a ₹300-crore worldwide phenomenon — will make her Hindi film debut opposite Ranveer.

She almost didn't say yes.

Reports suggest that Kalyani was initially reluctant to launch her Bollywood career with a zombie film. The genre felt niche, the leap felt risky. Then Ranveer Singh, wearing his producer hat, did what Ranveer does best: he picked up the phone himself. According to *Mid-day*, he walked her through the script's emotional architecture, the world-building, and exactly why her particular combination of vulnerability and ferocity was essential to the project. By the end of the conversation, she was in.

> "Pralay is not a zombie film in the way people imagine it. It's a survival story — about how far a man will go to protect his family in the most impossible circumstances." — Director Jai Mehta

For Kalyani, the timing is extraordinary. She walked the **Cannes 2026** red carpet in May, riding the global wave of *Lokah*'s success — the first Malayalam film to cross the ₹300-crore mark worldwide. Her portrayal of the mythological Kalliyankattu Neeli earned her the kind of acclaim that transcends language, and her fan base now stretches far beyond Kerala. Now she's crossing the language barrier entirely, stepping into the most expensive Hindi production of the year alongside the industry's reigning box office king.

## Not *Blindness*, Not Bollywood-as-Usual

Speculation had swirled for months that Pralay was an adaptation of José Saramago's celebrated 1995 novel *Blindness*. **Hansal Mehta** — filmmaker, producer, and Jai's father — shut that down in April.

> "It's an entirely original story developed by Jai and his co-writer Vishal Kapoor." — Hansal Mehta

The senior Mehta added that he'd seen the 2008 Hollywood adaptation starring Julianne Moore and Mark Ruffalo, and found it underwhelming — which is perhaps why his son chose to build a world from scratch instead.

What Pralay promises is something Indian cinema has genuinely never done at this scale: a dystopian, VFX-heavy, emotionally grounded thriller that merges physical sets with AI-driven visuals to create a post-apocalyptic landscape unlike anything shot on Indian soil. The production's extensive pre-production phase — months of world-building before a single shot is filmed — explains the ₹300-crore price tag.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

For NRI audiences who've been binging *The Last of Us* on HBO and rewatching *28 Days Later*, Pralay could be the first Indian film that speaks that visual language while telling a story rooted in desi emotional stakes. The family survival angle — protecting your own against impossible odds — is about as universal as storytelling gets, but giving it an Indian setting and Indian star power makes it genuinely unprecedented.

Director Jai Mehta, best known for co-helming the landmark series *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story* — which swept 11 of 14 nominations at the Filmfare OTT Awards — is making his feature film directorial debut with Pralay. It's a massive leap from the claustrophobic world of financial scams to an open, apocalyptic landscape. But Scam proved Mehta could make you feel the enormity of a story even in a small room. Now he has ₹300 crore and the end of the world to play with.

Shooting begins in August. Ranveer Singh is betting everything that Bollywood is ready for its first blockbuster apocalypse. And honestly? After *Dhurandhar*, would you bet against him?
